change.jurisdiction: EU; transposed in Germany as § 356a BGB
change.summary: Online stores selling to EU consumers must offer a clearly labelled, two-step electronic withdrawal function and confirm receipt on a durable medium. Applies to contracts concluded from 19 June 2026.

obligations.text: Provide a withdrawal function on the online interface.
obligations.quote: the trader shall ensure that the consumer can also exercise the right of withdrawal by means of a withdrawal function

obligations.text: Label it clearly and make it two-step (fill in, then confirm).
obligations.quote: The withdrawal function shall be labelled with the words 'withdraw contract here' or a corresponding unambiguous formulation in an easily legible manner

obligations.text: Send an acknowledgement on a durable medium.
obligations.quote: the trader shall communicate to the consumer without undue delay an acknowledgement of receipt of the withdrawal on a durable medium

reasons: You sell to consumers in 10 EU countries, so the EU consumer-rights rules apply to your distance contracts.
Your business is established in Germany, where the rule is § 356a BGB and is in force since 19 June 2026.

todos.text: Add a labelled, two-step withdrawal button to your storefront
todos.quote: the trader shall ensure that the consumer can also exercise the right of withdrawal by means of a withdrawal function

todos.text: Send an automatic confirmation email when a customer uses it
todos.quote: the trader shall communicate to the consumer without undue delay an acknowledgement of receipt of the withdrawal on a durable medium
